title: Refine weekly cutflow: canary cohorts, region-aware gates, and release-note atomizer
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Consolidate the weekly build cut process into a deterministic pipeline that produces a single RC artifact per channel, wires region-aware rollout gates, formalizes canary cohorts, and generates machine-readable + human release notes (the 'release-note atomizer').

Scope:
- Author deterministic cut job that picks successful CI candidate based on stability window and semantic-versioning policy.
- Enforce RC tagging naming: runtime-<MAJOR>.<MINOR>.<PATCH>-rc.<cut-number> and map to channel tags: 'stable', 'lts-<major>', 'edge'.
- Implement a rollout gate matrix evaluated at cut time (tests, infra health, telemetry thresholds, quota budget check) with explicit gate output logged to release metadata.
- Canary cohorts: add a configurable cohort scheduler (0.5%, 5%, 25%) per region with rollback hooks. Cohorts evaluate latency SLO, error-rate, and model-quality regression checks.
- Release-note atomizer: aggregate commits, PR descriptions, changelog fragments, CI test summaries, and known-issue annotations into structured JSON and a MD fallback for console and email. Include direct links to PRs, runbooks, and QA signoffs.

Acceptance criteria:
- Every weekly cut produces an artifact and a release-metadata.json containing: commit SHAs, RC tag, gating decision log, canary cohort config, and release-note-atomizer output.
- Canary rollout can be started/paused from Console with a single click and exposes metrics for each cohort in the Console dashboard.
- Rollback performs automated traffic shift to previous stable artifact within 10 minutes max TTL.
- Release notes publish automatically to the release-notes S3 bucket and appear in Console within 15 minutes of cut completion.

Trade-offs and rationale:
- Strong gating at cut time reduces downstream incidents but increases risk of skipping a release when infra is transiently noisy. To mitigate: gate criteria use rolling percentiles and allow a 'defer to on-call' flag that lets a human approve in edge cases.
- Cohort granularity increases orchestration complexity; to avoid an explosion of state we keep cohorts as simple percentage buckets per-region with a single rollout manager service that reuses existing autoscaler hooks.
- Atomized release notes prioritize machine-parsable fields for downstream automation (changelogs, release dashboards) over perfect prose; we add a human-editable MD layer for marketing/ops to refine after publishing.

Implementation plan (milestones):
1) 2026-03-10 to 2026-03-15: Build RC tag generator and cut job; emit release-metadata.json (MVP).
2) 2026-03-16 to 2026-03-19: Implement gating matrix evaluation and logging; add optional human override flow.
3) 2026-03-20 to 2026-03-28: Canary cohort scheduler, rollout manager hooks, and Console controls + cohort metrics.
4) 2026-03-29 to 2026-04-02: Release-note atomizer (structured JSON + MD fallback) and S3 publish pipeline.

Metrics for success:
- Time-to-cut (CI success -> RC artifact) < 30 minutes for 90th percentile.
- Mean time to detect post-cut regressions (via cohort telemetry) < 15 minutes.
- Percentage of weekly cuts with human override < 5% after first month.

Rollback plan: automated traffic shift to previous stable tag coordinated with autoscaler and cache invalidation. Manual rollback steps recorded in the runbook link below.

Runbooks and artifacts: see links.
